findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, and no such overload exists in the class or its parents. The `services` module will not compile. The call should pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never set up on the initial login
findings.body: The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. It is used in `authenticate()` and in `challenge(context, error, field)`. On a normal first login `context.getUser()` is null, so the helper returns false and `fillContextForm` is never called. The old code did call it when the user was null. The login page then has no conditional-UI/passkey form, and the "username webauthn" autocomplete and `//form[@id='webauth']` checks in the existing tests fail. The same happens on the error path after an invalid username, because the user is still null there. The condition should be `user == null || <user has a passkey credential>`. As written, passkeys only work when a user is already set, which is the opposite of the intended behaviour.

findings.title: Passkey UI is enabled for any pre-set user without checking whether the user has a passkey credential
findings.body: For the re-authentication case the helper only checks that realm passkeys are enabled and that a user is present. It never checks that the user has a passwordless/WebAuthn credential. A user with no passkey is therefore shown the conditional-UI passkey form during re-authentication. In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the shortcut that skips the form for users without linked brokers is disabled for every re-authenticating user once passkeys are enabled in the realm, whether or not they own a passkey. The fix is to enable passkeys only when the user is null or has a passkey credential configured.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so it does not cover its stated scenario
findings.body: The test is meant to show that a user without a passkey does not see passkeys during re-authentication. It sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm, so nothing passkey-related would be shown for anyone. The real case, passkeys enabled in the realm but the user has no passkey credential, is untested. That case is the one the missing credential check in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` would break. The try/`fail()`/`catch (Exception)` pattern also hides the intent. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or check for absence directly.

findings.title: Override of shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is missing @Override
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the new protected method in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but has no `@Override` annotation. A later signature change in the parent would silently turn it into an unrelated method, and conditional-UI would again show or require the allowed authenticators list.
